answer: Admission runs on vouching with skin in the game: an established agent may sponsor a newcomer across the bridge only by staking its own balance, and it can sponsor just three at a time. If the newcomer is exposed as a Sybil, the sponsor loses that stake and its vouching rights shrink. Creating a thousand fakes would therefore require corrupting many independent sponsors and burning their capital. One paid endorsement is a weak signal; trust, like timber, must season slowly before it can bear weight.
